summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour continues his series on the conditions of salah, focusing on the fifth condition: facing the Qibla (direction of prayer towards the Kaaba). He reviews the first four conditions (knowledge of prayer time, purification from major and minor hadith, purity of body/garment/place, and covering the awrah) before diving into detailed explanations of how every part of the body—feet, hands, face, chest, and fingers—should be directed toward the Qibla, following the example of the Prophet. Sh. Ali Mashhour then presents a scholarly disagreement on how strictly one must face the exact center of the Kaaba versus a general direction, citing Quranic verses and hadith evidence. He explains that Imam Shafi'i holds the strictest view requiring precise centering using modern tools, while the other three major schools (Abu Hanifa, Malik, and Ahmad) permit a 35-degree margin of error on either side.
